The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, review and verification (reviewing the completeness, accuracy, and compliance of budget estimates, verifying bases and assumptions, analyzing monthly budget and accounting reports, and identifying anomalies and trends); second, analysis and recommendations (cost analysis, cost-benefit comparison, funding source and allocation recommendations, and budget adjustment recommendations, consolidated into a budget plan usable for decisions); third, reporting and execution tracking (preparing routine and special budget reports, interpreting budget instructions and formulating execution policies, coordinating budget adjustments with managers, and tracking execution). All three share the same analytical chain centered on the basis and evidence.
Review and verification

Collect departmental budget needs and historical data → review the completeness and accuracy of estimates → verify whether bases and assumptions are consistent → analyze monthly budget and accounting reports → identify anomalies and trends → record doubtful points and ask for guidance.
Analysis and recommendations

Conduct cost analysis and cost-benefit comparison → assess funding needs and feasibility → consolidate the budget and form funding application recommendations → compare operating options or alternative financing methods → discuss adjustments with managers → submit a budget plan and basis usable for decisions.

Prepare routine and special budget reports, interpret budget instructions and formulate execution policies, consolidate the budget and track execution, and feed back deviations and adjustment recommendations with documentation.

Budget analysts center on reviewing budget estimates, cost analysis, and budget reports; accountants and auditors are responsible for bookkeeping and audit judgments; financial managers are responsible for institutional financial strategy and fund management; financial and investment analysts are responsible for investment research and recommendations; management analysts are responsible for organizational process and efficiency analysis; tellers are responsible for cash and counter business. Similar names or working in the same finance function do not mean responsibilities and authority are interchangeable.
Core purpose

Under procedures, rules, and budget constraints, translate departmental resource needs into consistently based, comparable, and executable budgets and cost analyses, provide a basis for funding application and allocation decisions, and support execution control.
Main objects and basis

The objects are departmental needs, budget and accounting reports, cost and benefit data, and funding applications; the basis is applicable regulations, institutional rules, appropriation terms, and data assumptions. In mainland China, government budgets and related department units are verified against the current 2018 amendment of the Budget Law for preparation, review, approval, execution, and adjustment; enterprise internal budgets are verified against the applicable accounting system, governance, and unit authorization, and government budget procedures are not generalized to all enterprise budgets.
Core process

Collect needs, review estimates and bases, analyze reports and trends, conduct cost and benefit analysis, consolidate budgets and recommendations, prepare reports, and track execution and adjustments.
Main outputs

Consistently based and verifiable budgets and cost analyses, funding application and allocation recommendations, routine and special budget reports, budget execution tracking and deviation statements, and complete basis and adjustment records.
Responsible parties

Budget analysts are responsible for their analyses and recommendations; budget approval, accounting treatment, and external commitments are determined by the positions and institutions that actually have the authority, and duties may overlap but authority cannot be presumed from the occupational title.
Authority and approval

Preparation, review, approval, submission, and funding commitments are verified separately against actual rules and position authorization; training records prove learning experience and do not automatically grant authorization. Statutory budget adjustments under Articles 67/69 of the government Budget Law are approved by the corresponding people's congress or its standing committee, Article 72 transfers follow fiscal rules, and Article 73 has separate filing; enterprise budgets follow unit governance, and not all adjustments and submissions are uniformly written as requiring approval.
Conclusion boundary

The analysis states "under this basis and these assumptions, what the resource needs and cost-benefit look like"; it does not equal an approval conclusion, nor does it replace audit and final account conclusions, and it will be revised as policy, operations, and data are updated.

Budget analysts (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 13-2031.00, Budget Analysts) review the completeness and accuracy of budget estimates and their compliance with procedures and rules and analyze budget and accounting reports. Daily work includes: analyzing monthly budget and accounting reports of each department to maintain expenditure control; providing advice and technical assistance on cost analysis, fund allocation, and budget preparation; reviewing operating budgets and analyzing trends affecting budget needs; consolidating and analyzing accounting records and other data to determine the resources needed to implement programs; consolidating budgets and recommending approval or non-approval of funding requests; consulting with managers to ensure budgets are adjusted as programs change; directing the preparation of routine and special budget reports; interpreting budget instructions and formulating execution policies; and conducting cost-benefit analysis to compare operating options, review funding applications, or explore alternative financing methods. It bears analysis and recommendation responsibility, but does not replace the competent department in approving budgets or deciding appropriations.

BU01 fictional, same 2026 first quarter, RMB yuan, expenditures positive and consistently based: A approved budget 100,000, actual 110,000; B approved budget 80,000, draft actual 9 (labeled in yuan), and the original consolidation table states the actual is 9 ten-thousand yuan. BU02 the same one-year options: option A initial cost 6,000, known maintenance cost 1,000, estimated savings 9,000; option B initial cost 4,000, maintenance cost unknown, estimated savings 7,000. The savings values are all estimates, and whether the A and B estimates can be realized and whether the options are approved are unknown. The given rule is net benefit = estimated savings − initial cost − maintenance cost, and net benefit rate = net benefit ÷ total cost.
